title: Capacity Planning, Autoscaling & Performance at Scale

scenes.heading: Capacity & Autoscaling
scenes.narration: Capacity planning and autoscaling keep a platform fast under load while avoiding the waste of paying for idle resources.

scenes.heading: Inputs to capacity planning
bullets: Lead time to provision more capacity
scenes.narration: Sound capacity planning starts with knowing your current utilization and how much headroom remains. It folds in growth forecasts and seasonal spikes so you are not caught out by a predictable surge. It distinguishes peak demand from average, since sizing for the average will fail at the peak, and it accounts for how long provisioning new capacity actually takes.

scenes.heading: Reactive vs predictive scaling
scenes.narration: Reactive scaling responds after load has already risen, which is simple to set up but always lags behind a sudden spike. Predictive scaling provisions ahead of a forecast, so it handles known events like month-end batches gracefully. Predictive works well only when your demand signals are reliable, so many teams combine both.

scenes.heading: An autoscaling policy
scenes.code:
autoscaling:
  min_workers: 2
  max_workers: 40
  target_metric: pending_tasks_per_worker
  target_value: 5
  scale_up:
    cooldown_seconds: 60
  scale_down:
    cooldown_seconds: 300   # scale down slowly to avoid thrash
scenes.narration: This policy keeps between two and forty workers and scales to hold about five pending tasks per worker. It scales up quickly on a short cooldown so users are not left waiting during a surge. It scales down slowly on a longer cooldown to avoid thrashing, where the cluster repeatedly shrinks and grows and wastes startup time.

scenes.heading: The scaling feedback loop
scenes.narration: Autoscaling runs as a continuous feedback loop. It measures current load, compares it to the target, and adds or removes workers accordingly. Cooldown periods prevent overreaction, and then the loop re-measures so the system settles smoothly rather than oscillating.

scenes.text: Size for the peak, scale for the average, and set floors and ceilings so autoscaling can't starve you or bankrupt you.
scenes.narration: Plan for the peak, let autoscaling ride the average, and always set sensible floors and ceilings so scaling can neither starve your workloads nor blow up your bill.
